feature: About The 99 — the reference page, its gate and its figures
note: One route, and the close-out's job is the page a reader actually gets rather than the route existing. Three rows, and they are ONE reader state rather than three. The page draws differently for a reader at version 0, one who is behind and one who is current, but the acknowledged version lives in `user_prefs` — no URL reaches those states, and `?next=` sets only the dismiss destination. The fixture account is in exactly one of them, so these rows differ in what they photograph (the head, the figures, the destination clause) and not in who is reading. The other two states are held by `about-page.test.tsx`, which renders `seen={0}`, `seen={ABOUT_VERSION}` and a version-2 page with one entry marked; a walk wanting the real thing would write the row and put it back, in the shape `probe:review` uses for its collection edits. The account menu row is deliberately NOT here. It is the page's permanent entry point and the one surface outside `/about` this feature changed, but every verb in this script reaches page content through `onPage`, which scopes to `<main>` — and the shell's account trigger sits outside it by construction. A row for it could only be written by defeating that scope, which is the rule that stopped two probes measuring the shell while naming a page. It is covered instead by `account-menu.test.tsx`, which asserts the row's position, its link, the roving wrap past it and its busy state, and by the close-out walk. No `shares` block: every figure mounts an app component in ONE place, so there is no second route to be the same as — the sameness question this feature has is whether a figure matches the surface it documents, which is what `figures.tsx` asserts per figure and what this sheet shows in a glance.
